clusters.label: High electrical conductivity (ionic)
clusters.definition: High electrical conductivity associated with mobile ions.
clusters.reason: The evidence identifies conduction in cement pore solution and an ionic liquid; material identities remain claim-specific.

clusters.label: High electrical conductivity (electronic)
clusters.definition: High ability to conduct electrical current through electronic carriers.
clusters.reason: These mentions describe the same conductivity property in electronic conducting materials. Different carrier-transport explanations and samples remain attached to their claims.

clusters.label: High electrical conductivity (predicted electronic)
clusters.definition: High electronic electrical conductivity obtained from theoretical calculations.
clusters.reason: The supplied evidence explicitly identifies calculations or DFT/Boltzmann transport studies, distinguishing these predictions from experimentally reported conductivity.

clusters.label: Ionic thermoelectric effect
clusters.reason: Both explicitly identify the ionic thermoelectric process. The ionogel's additional piezoionic effect and combined voltage outcome do not change this component concept.

clusters.label: High Seebeck coefficient (ionic)
clusters.definition: High thermoelectric voltage response per temperature difference associated with ionic transport.
clusters.reason: Cement pore ions and engineered ionic migration channels explicitly establish ionic thermoelectric contexts.

clusters.label: High Seebeck coefficient (electronic)
clusters.definition: High electronic thermoelectric voltage response per temperature difference.
clusters.reason: These describe electronic thermopower in solid thermoelectric materials, supported by measurements, resistivity, carrier transport, or electronic-band contexts. No explicit opposite coefficient signs are supplied; material and strain details remain claim-specific.

clusters.label: High Seebeck coefficient (predicted electronic)
clusters.definition: High electronic thermopower determined through theoretical transport calculations.
clusters.reason: Titles, conditions, and evidence explicitly establish DFT or calculated transport contexts. These predictions are kept separate from the other reported electronic coefficients.

clusters.label: High Seebeck coefficient (hybrid thermoelectrochemical device)
clusters.definition: High device thermovoltage per temperature difference arising from the stated hybrid mechanisms.
clusters.reason: The evidence explicitly attributes device performance to hybrid mechanisms involving electrolyte and electrodes; it does not establish equivalence to a purely ionic, electronic, or thermogalvanic coefficient.

clusters.label: Ionic thermoelectric materials
clusters.definition: A class of materials exhibiting thermoelectric responses through ionic processes.
clusters.reason: All labels denote the same material class, whether discussed through figure-of-merit applicability, combination with pyroelectrics, or a proposed ionogel application. They do not identify the individual samples as equivalent.
